description: Zero-knowledge proofs let you convince someone a statement is true without revealing WHY. Apply this to mathematics: a zero-knowledge proof of a theorem T convinces the verifier that T is provable in PA without revealing any step of the proof. Conjecture: Every theorem provable in Peano Arithmetic has a zero-knowledge proof whose communication complexity is polynomial in the length of the theorem statement (not the proof). This follows from the PCP theorem combined with the fact that PA-proofs can be arithmetized. The zero-knowledge protocol: (1) Prover commits to each proof step using a collision-resistant hash. (2) Verifier randomly challenges one proof step. (3) Prover opens that step and shows it follows from the axioms. Repeating O(k) times gives soundness error 2^{-k}. The proof is zero-knowledge because the verifier only sees one random step per challenge. Test: implement a zero-knowledge proof system for propositional tautologies and prove that a verifier learns nothing beyond the validity of the tautology. Impact: mathematicians can certify results without revealing their methods — a mathematical equivalent of sealed-bid auctions for proof strategies.
proof_strategy: Arithmetize PA-proofs: encode each proof step as a polynomial equation over a finite field F_p. Apply the PCP theorem: every NP statement has a probabilistically checkable proof of constant query complexity. Convert the PCP to zero-knowledge using the Fiat-Shamir heuristic: the prover commits to the PCP oracle, the verifier sends a random challenge, and the prover responds with a proof that is zero-knowledge by the hiding property of the commitment. Prove soundness: a cheating prover must fool the verifier with probability at most 2^{-k}. Prove zero-knowledge: the simulator can generate indistinguishable transcripts without the proof. Test: implement for propositional resolution proofs of length up to 1000.
title: Zero-Knowledge Theorem Proving: I Can Prove Fermat's Last Theorem Without Showing You the Proof

Conjecture: Non-well-founded proofs form a convergent fixed point under a natural topolog: the space of proof trees with the tree topology is a Scott domain, and self-referential proofs correspond to infinite chains whose lub is a valid proof. A proof that references itself is like a recursive function: it converges if the self-reference occurs at a strictly smaller ordinal. Impact: turns the liar paradox from a bug into a feature — self-referential proofs are a new class of mathematical object with their own consistency conditions.

Define ordinal height: oh(P) = sup{oh(Q)+1 : Q is a subproof of P}. A NWFP is valid if oh(P) is a well-defined ordinal.
